outputs.L1: The invention relates to a pressure-measuring device for converting mechanical or hydraulic pressure into a measurement signal and transmitting the measurement signal to a remote evaluation unit. The invention is characterized by a fastening device (1) for securing the pressure-measuring device to a machine housing of a motor or pump; a transmitter head (4), arranged on a measuring-device head (3) of the pressure-measuring device and connectable to a light source via a first optical fiber (25); a receiver head (5), arranged on the measuring-device head (3) opposite the transmitter head (4), for receiving light emitted by the transmitter head (4) along a light path through the measuring-device head (3), and connectable to the evaluation unit via a second optical fiber (26); and a measuring element (14) that, when subjected to mechanical or hydraulic pressure, is displaceable on the measuring-device head (3) into the light path between the transmitter head (4) and the receiver head (5).
outputs.L2: The invention concerns a pressure-sensing apparatus that transforms mechanical or hydraulic pressure into a measurement signal and transmits that signal to a remotely located evaluation unit. The apparatus includes a fastening device (1) for securing it to the machine housing of a motor or pump. A transmitter head (4), mounted on the measuring device head (3), can be connected to a light source by a first optical fiber (25). A receiver head (5) is also mounted on the measuring device head (3), opposite the transmitter head (4), so that it receives light transmitted along a light path through the measuring device head (3). The receiver head (5) can be linked to the evaluation unit by a second optical fiber (26). In response to mechanical or hydraulic pressure, a measuring element (14) can move into the light path between the transmitter head (4) and the receiver head (5).
outputs.L3:
The pressure-measuring device converts mechanical or hydraulic pressure into an optical measurement signal that can be transmitted to a remote evaluation unit. A fastening device securely mounts the pressure-measuring device to the machine housing of a motor or pump.

Within the measuring device head, a transmitter head is connected to a light source by a first optical fiber. The transmitter head emits light along a defined path through the measuring device head. Positioned opposite the transmitter head, a receiver head detects the transmitted light and is connected to the remote evaluation unit by a second optical fiber.

When mechanical or hydraulic pressure acts on the device, a measuring element moves into the light path. This movement changes the intensity or other detectable characteristics of the light received by the receiver head. The resulting optical signal is transmitted through the second optical fiber to the evaluation unit, where it is processed to determine the applied pressure.
outputs.L4:
The invention relates to a pressure-measuring device for monitoring mechanical or hydraulic pressure, particularly in machines such as motors, pumps, compressors, and similar units. The device converts a pressure-dependent displacement into an optical signal that can be transmitted to and evaluated at a location remote from the machine.

The device includes an optical transmitter head and an optical receiver head arranged opposite one another on or adjacent to a machine housing. The transmitter head is connected to a light source by a first optical fiber, while the receiver head is connected by a second optical fiber to a remote evaluation unit. The two heads define a light path through which light emitted by the transmitter normally passes to the receiver.

A pressure-responsive measuring element is mounted on the machine housing and is exposed, directly or indirectly, to the pressure to be measured. Depending on the application, the measuring element may respond to hydraulic pressure within a fluid chamber or to mechanical pressure generated by a moving or loaded machine component. The element is positioned so that its pressure-dependent movement changes the amount of light transmitted between the transmitter and receiver heads.

When the applied pressure increases, the measuring element is displaced into, or farther into, the light path. This displacement partially or completely interrupts, attenuates, redirects, or otherwise modifies the light reaching the receiver head. When the pressure decreases, the measuring element moves in the opposite direction, allowing a greater amount of light to reach the receiver. The resulting variation in optical intensity therefore represents the magnitude or state of the pressure acting on the measuring element.

The receiver head couples the modified optical signal into the second optical fiber, which carries it to the evaluation unit. The evaluation unit may convert the received light intensity into a corresponding electrical pressure signal, compare the signal with one or more threshold values, display the measured pressure, record pressure variations, or initiate a warning or control operation if an abnormal condition is detected. Depending on the configuration, the device can provide continuous pressure measurement or simply indicate whether a predetermined pressure limit has been reached.

Because the sensing region operates optically, electrical components do not have to be placed directly at the measuring point. This arrangement reduces sensitivity to electromagnetic interference and permits monitoring in locations subject to vibration, heat, moisture, contamination, or restricted access. The use of optical fibers also enables the light source and evaluation electronics to be positioned at a safe and convenient distance from the machine.

The opposing transmitter and receiver heads may be secured directly to the machine housing or mounted in a separate support attached to the housing. Their relative positions can be selected so that the optical response corresponds to the expected movement range of the measuring element. Calibration may be performed by relating particular received-light levels to known pressure values. The geometry of the measuring element and light path may likewise be adapted to provide a substantially linear response, a stepped response, or a switching response at a selected pressure.

In operation, light is supplied through the first optical fiber to the transmitter head and projected across the defined gap toward the receiver head. Pressure acting on the measuring element causes a proportional or otherwise predetermined displacement of that element within the gap. The displacement changes optical transmission, and the changed signal is conveyed through the second optical fiber to the remote evaluation unit. In this manner, mechanical or hydraulic pressure within a motor, pump, or other machine can be monitored reliably without requiring electrical pressure-sensing circuitry at the point of measurement.

### The Power of “The”

“The” is one of the smallest and most frequently used words in the English language. Known as the definite article, it identifies a particular person, place, object, or idea. Saying “the book” suggests a specific book, while “a book” could mean any book.

Although it often goes unnoticed, “the” brings clarity and precision to communication. It helps listeners and readers understand when something is unique, already known, or especially important. From “the sun” to “the future,” this simple word shapes meaning in countless sentences.

Its power lies in its subtlety: “the” rarely attracts attention, yet English would be far less clear without it.

counterfactuals.prompt: Write a patent-style abstract for a pressure-measuring device that converts mechanical or hydraulic pressure into an optical measuring signal transmitted to a remote evaluation unit.
counterfactuals.output: A pressure-measuring device converts mechanical or hydraulic pressure into an optical measuring signal for transmission to a remote evaluation unit. The device comprises a pressure-sensitive element that undergoes displacement, deformation, or a change in force in response to applied pressure, and an optical transducer operatively coupled to the pressure-sensitive element. The optical transducer modulates at least one characteristic of incident light, including intensity, wavelength, phase, polarization, or propagation path, as a function of the applied pressure. An optical waveguide transmits the modulated light from the pressure-measuring device to the remote evaluation unit, which determines a pressure value from the modulated characteristic. The device may include temperature compensation, a reference optical path, and calibration data for correcting environmental and component-related variations. By locating electrical signal-processing components remotely from the pressure-sensing location, the device provides pressure measurement in environments subject to electromagnetic interference, elevated electrical potential, explosive atmospheres, or restricted access.
counterfactuals.label: cf_1

counterfactuals.prompt: Describe an invention comprising a housing fastening device, opposing optical transmitter and receiver heads connected by fibers, and a pressure-responsive measuring element that moves into the light path.
counterfactuals.output: The invention is a fiber-optic pressure sensor mounted in a housing by a fastening device. Opposing optical transmitter and receiver heads are positioned within the housing and coupled to respective optical fibers, thereby defining a light path between the heads. A pressure-responsive measuring element, such as a diaphragm or bellows, moves in response to applied pressure and enters the light path to attenuate or interrupt the transmitted light. The resulting change in light received through the receiver fiber provides an optical indication of the pressure.
